newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Union wants interdict against Randfontein.
newsitem.headline: Union wants interdict against Randfontein.

text.p: The National Union of Mineworkers said on Thursday it would seek an urgent court interdict against Randfontein Estate Gold Mine over the planned retrenchment of 4,000 workers.
The union (NUM) said it would seek the interdict after the company reneged on an earlier agreement delaying the retrenchment of the workers until the end of June.
Randfontein said earlier that it could not delay the planned axing of the workers.
"With each day that passes, the prejudice it suffers increases, as well as the possibility of further job losses," owner JCI Ltd said in a statement.
The NUM said it had committed to a process of looking into alternatives to the retrenchment of the workers and discussions on acceptable package.

"In view of the arrogance projected by the company we will approach the Labour Court and ask for an urgent court interdict against Randfontein...until the consultation process is properly done," it said.
JCI said earlier that consultations with NUM had resulted in agreement on all issues except the severance packages payable and a final list of affected employees.
It said the mine had complied with all the requirements of the Labour Relations Act and was entitled to continue with the retrenchments.

Randfontein produced 4,392 kg of gold in the March quarter compared to 5,100 kg in the December quarter. It plunged into a loss of 2.86 million rand, well down on the previous quarter's 43.83 million rand profit.
